study_guide.title: Cane Reads the Clouds

pages.text: Cane the Weather Dog flopped onto the soft green grass and looked up at the sky. "Do you know my favorite thing to do? Read the clouds!" "First," said Cane, "here's a secret. Clouds are not made of cotton or fluff. They are made of millions of tiny water droplets — the same droplets from the water cycle, all floating together!" "Now, let's learn their names. Clouds come in different shapes, and each shape tells us something."
pages.ask: Can you point up at a cloud in the sky?

pages.text: Cane pointed to a big puffy cloud. "That fluffy one, like a cotton ball, is a cumulus cloud. Cumulus clouds usually mean a nice, fair day. Perfect for playing outside!"
Then Cane pointed low and wide. "See that flat, gray one, spreading across the whole sky? That's a stratus cloud. Stratus clouds can bring a little drizzle, so you might want an umbrella."
pages.ask: Can you spread your arms out wide and flat, like a stratus cloud?

pages.text: Cane looked way, way up high. "And those thin, wispy ones, like feathers? Those are cirrus clouds. They are very high up, and usually mean fair weather too." "Cumulus, stratus, cirrus," said Cane happily. "Puffy, flat, and wispy. Once you know them, you can read the sky like a real weather scientist!"

Then Cane's ears perked up. Off in the distance, a cloud was growing tall and dark. "Uh oh," said Cane. "That big, tall, dark cloud is a storm cloud. When you see one growing like that, a thunderstorm might be coming." Cane stood up. "So here's the smart thing to do. When a storm cloud grows tall and dark, tell a grown-up and be ready to go inside. Remember — when thunder roars, go indoors!"
pages.ask: Can you name the tall, dark cloud that brings storms?

pages.text: The tall cloud drifted far away, and the sky filled with puffy cumulus again. Cane wagged his tail. "The clouds are the sky's weather report. And now, YOU can read them!" "Great job, weather watcher," said Cane. "You learned to read the clouds. You are weather-ready!"

study_guide.rule: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets, and their shape tells us what weather is coming.
